title: The Dry, Cozy Den
markdown:
Rain whispered on Willow Creek Farm, a soft lullaby. Inside Calla and Sprig’s mossy den a tiny drip, drip, drip. The floor felt a little damp.

“Oh dear,” Calla whispered, smile dimming. “Our floor is getting wet.” Sprig mumbled, nose twitching.

Calla tried a wide maple leaf. Water flowed away and still found the moss. Sprig offered shiny foil; drops slid off and pooled. A fluffy dandelion puff let the dampness seep through. Soggy.

Dr. Ada arrived with a warm smile. “Ah. A little dampness.” From her satchel, a wisp of soft cotton wool. They watched water melt into the fluffy fibres, disappearing — not magic, only the fluff taking the drip in and holding it. “See how it welcomes the water?” Fuzzy felt did the same.

“So the soft fluff holds the water?” Sprig’s eyes bright.

“Exactly. Absorbent materials. Special helpers.”

With new hope they placed cotton wool and felt under the leak. Drip, drip, drip. This time the water was welcomed and held. The den floor stayed dry and warm.

“It’s working! Our den is cozy again!”

“Absorbent,” Sprig whispered, the word soft on his tongue. Calla nestled into the dry floor. The rain kept singing. They did not need a lecture on tomorrow’s discoveries. The drip had somewhere kind to go, and that was enough for a den, and for sleep.
